page: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual machine provisioned on an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The instance features a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled to deliver two dedicated vCPUs. Memory is configured at 16.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Bundled storage comprises a 480 GB local NVMe SSD, and networking includes one complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration. The CPU implements 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache, supporting extended instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptographic extensions including AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

Benchmark data displays a marked contrast between single-core performance and parallel execution throughput. In stress-ng single-core tests, the server achieves top-tier results with a score of 3429.67, complemented by strong Geekbench single-core performance (2116.0) and rapid compression capabilities (31.96 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip). However, bounded by its two-vCPU count, parallel execution is modest; Geekbench multi-core performance places in the lower quartile at 3772.0, with PassMark overall CPU arriving at 5983.03. Memory read and write bandwidth for large blocks (256 MB) remains balanced in the middle tier at 76.99 GB/sec and 69.10 GB/sec respectively, though cached 16 KB read-only throughput sits in the bottom quartile at 328.38 GB/sec.

Because of the 8.0 GB per core resource density, this server provides a memory-oriented operational model within a low core-count profile. Tasks involving high concurrent execution, large compilation pipelines (Clang score of 4398.0), or heavy parallel serving are hardware-constrained by the single physical core. Conversely, workloads that prioritize strong single-thread execution, moderate local NVMe capacity, and generous per-thread memory capacity benefit from its balanced profile. Suitable workloads include in-memory key-value caching, single-process background workers, lightweight transactional databases, text-processing services, and modest ETL or CI/CD tasks.
description: Vultr voc-s-2c-16gb-480s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute virtual server powered by an AMD EPYC x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. It offers 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core, coupled with 16.0 GB of system memory and 480 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The CPU package incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache alongside modern instruction sets, including AVX-512 and hardware crypto primitives. Benchmarks show top-tier single-core compute and solid sequential compression results, whereas overall multi-core throughput and compiling metrics reflect the physical dual-thread limitation. Memory bandwidth registers at balanced midrange rates for uncached workloads. Given the 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU allocation, this configuration suits memory-heavy lightweight workloads, small databases, cache nodes, and single-threaded tasks needing fast local NVMe storage.
